recipes.name: Dad's Cheesy Bacon Wrapped Meat Loaf
ingredients_raw: 8 ounces sharp Cheddar cheese, cut into quarters

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Combine ground beef, eggs and 2 tablespoons of ketchup in a large bowl. Mix well, then add bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, garlic powder, salt, oregano, basil, pepper, and onion. Set mixture aside. Line the bottom of a 9x13 inch pan with bacon, widthwise. Place half of the meat mixture across the top of the bacon. Lay 3 of the 4 pieces of Cheddar cheese across the center of the meat, lengthwise. Cover the cheese with the second half of the meat mixture and mold the meat into a loaf shape. Pull the ends of the bacon up and around the loaf. Spread 1 tablespoon of ketchup thinly over the loaf.

Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, about 60 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C). Remove from the oven.

Cut the final piece of Cheddar cheese into slices and place on top of the meat loaf. Return the meat loaf to the oven and continue baking until the cheese is melted, about 5 minutes. Remove from the oven and allow the meat loaf to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Dad's Cheesy Bacon Wrapped Meat Loaf
raw_recipe.description: Meat loaf that is covered in bacon and oozing with Cheddar cheese is sure to be a crowd pleaser!

review.reviewBody: I've found this is a great idea for picky men... men love anything wrapped in cheese and bacon! I did these in large muffin tins (it made six little muffins) because it cooks faster, serves more neatly, and is easier to wrap the bacon! I also added about a tablespoon of worcestershire sauce to keep it moist, and because it is such a good flavor with the beef. Next time i would use a few less bread crumbs, because the flavor of the bread crumbs was a bit overpowering. AWESOME recipe.

With slight changes, this was excellent!!! I used 1/4c bread crumbs (with a little italian seasoning) BBQ sauce instead of ketchup, made a 1 lb loaf with green onions, green bell pepper, dry mustard and used 3 pieces of real bacon, cut in half and just put on top. then about a tablespoon of bbq sauce on top of the bacon, into oven for an hour. I also mixed all the dry ingredients in a bowl, added the egg, while keeping the hamburger in the fridge. At the last minute, I added the hamburger, quickly blended and put a half a cup of shredded cheese into the middle. This kept its shape nicely because I kept it in the fridge. I would not add the cheese on top again because it seemed to just melt off. I did add about 1/8 tsp more on seasonings except the garlic powder, just added 2 cloves of zested garlic. I may add just a little more bbq sauce to the actual meatloaf mix next time, but a keeper!!! Great base recipe!

I give this recipe high marks for it's great flavor and relative ease to make. I do have a few substitutions I made however. I use fresh basil, oregano, and finely minced fresh garlic. One other substitution is Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce instead of ketchup it seems to add a certain zest that I prefer. I use the fresh vs powder because I grow these herbs. I also add two extra strips of bacon across the top and weave them into the slices coming up and around the meatloaf. (I like bacon) :) PS: In order to not have it be greasy use one of the new meatloaf pans with a rack so you can lift it out easily plus it can be raised slightly to allow the bacon grease to drip to the bottom of the pan away from the meatloaf.

Absolutely the finest meatloaf recipe I have ever come across! Bravo to your dear ‘ole Dad. God bless him! I added a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce to the recipe and instead of breadcrumbs, I used three crushed Ryvita "Muesli Crunch" version, rye crispbread crackers. (I think they work better than plain bread crumbs. as well as adding special flavour and texture.) Bacon and old cheddar cheese--how can you lose? It's certainly not just for men. lol

I have three grown men in my household and they all LOVED this. The only change I made was to coat the bacon wrapped meatloaf in brown sugar to caramelize it. I brushed on the ketchup after it baked for 30 minutes. It came out amazing! I think next time I might make it in individual sizes, so each bite has a bit of bacon and cheese in it! 

The guys said this was the best meatloaf EVER! Better than Grandma's, and that is saying a LOT. I was also requested to make this every other day, hahahaha.

My (now husband) asks me to make this on a regular basis! I tried it when we were first dating & it is on our short list of favorites! I skip the ketchup & only use bbq - Sweet Baby Rays is our favorite. I typically add more bbq in the mix too. I add extra onions & garlic and drizzle more bbq on top. Thanks to the previous reviews, I also followed their recommendations to skip the ketchup, add more bacon strips on top (my loaf is usually too big to 'wrap' bacon around the loaf so just have 4 on bottom & 4 on top). This needs garlic mashed potatoes served on the side!

I added Worcestershire sauce, and substituted panko 1/2 cup, for some of the breadcrumbs and added savory spice. Also used dried minced onion (about 1 TBSP) instead of fresh.
This has been a hit for 6+ years!

My husband and I made this for dinner and the only thing we did different was use big slice of pepperjack cheese on the first row. We put ketchup on the meatloaf before the bacon is folded together. After cooking for an hour we made a topping sauce of ketchup and bbq sauce and brown sugar and it was amazing. Great flavors. Must try.

I loved the idea of the recipe. The first time, I wasn't thrilled with the outcome. The second time, I chopped the raw bacon and mixed it into the raw ground beef, and cut the cheese into large cubes (maybe 1/2 inch) and mixed those in. I cooked as directed, sprinkled some cheese on top at the end, and it was great. The bacon flavor permeated the meat, rather that just sitting on top, and there were little bursts of cheese throughout the loaf.
My family enjoyed this meatloaf. The second time I made it, I sautéed the onion before adding it to the mixture. I also replaced the ketchup with barbecue sauce. It’s a keeper .

Made this for the family tonight!
Used cubed American cheese inside with two broken up Kraft singles slices (Also used 3 slices of Kraft singles for the cheese on top) but other than that, I followed the recipe exactly and used my meatloaf pan with the drain thing. 
Turned out AWESOME!!! 
Even the three boys (15 yrs,10 yrs, & 5 yrs) loved it!
Will definitely make this recipe again!
Thank you!
Easy, meaty, cheesy and great as leftover couldn`t be any better. I did use bar-b-que sauce not ketchup. A weeknight Keeper!

Didn’t have eggs so I used two dollops of sour cream. But w the cheese bacon and breadcrumbs I am literally dying to eat this! I only gave it a four because I haven’t tasted it yet and I would’ve anyway cause there’s always room for improvement
I flattered out the mixture then I put a bunch of shredded cheese in the middle then rolled it up using the parchment paper I laid the beef flat on then put it right in the pan .Awesome
Delicious but super greasy. Although...needs more bacon to wrap haha
I sliced off enough for dinner and put the rest in the fridge. Sliced it the next day and grilled it and made a burger. Arguably better the next day!

My dad doesn't like meatloaf, but enjoyed this recipe! I used half bread crumbs and half panko, which adds a certain level of fluffiness that's nice. Worcestershire sauce would be great mixed into the meat, and prepared horseradish would be GREAT on the serving you have! Pairs very well with oven roasted creamer potatoes and oven roasted broccoli!
Loved the recipe. I added more vegetables and I added jalapenos. Not too many. Really enjoyed the little bite it gave it. can't wait for leftovers tomorrow.
My whole family loved it, this is the 3rd one I've made. Wouldn't change a thing but I jist have to have a smaller portion cause of my high cholesterol
Even my picky eater loved this recipe. The only thing I changed was removing the onion as no one in my family likes it.
